Team — forwarding Acme's follow-up. They want concise, procurement-friendly language for two ask items. Draft answers below (my first pass). Please review and suggest edits — legal/product guidance particularly welcome for the training wording.

Draft (for Acme):
- Default request-log retention: 30 days. Customers on Dedicated/Private can configure retention to 0-3650 days per contract.
- Full request payload (prompts/responses): retained 90 days by default for debugging and abuse investigations; not used for model training unless customer explicitly opts in; can be deleted earlier on request or via retention policy.
- Training: Redwood does not use customer content to train or fine-tune public models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a documented agreement; we may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry to improve service quality.

Attachments I plan to send: Redwood_SIG_Response_2026-03-11.pdf and a simple data-retention-table.xlsx mapping defaults and configurable windows.

If no objections, I'll finalize and send to Acme tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Monica

Hi Jane,

Thanks for the quick follow-up. Please find our concise answers below and the signed response attached (Redwood_SIG_Response_2026-03-11.pdf). I've also attached a short data retention table for easy reference.

Short answers (for procurement):
- Request logs (routing/latency/error metadata): default retention 30 days for Hosted API. Customers using Dedicated or Private deployments can configure retention from 0 to 3,650 days via contract and console controls. Request logs are metadata only (no full prompt content).

- Full request payloads (prompts, responses, attachments): default retention 90 days for Hosted API to support debugging, abuse investigations, and support tickets. Dedicated/Private customers may set payload retention to 0 days (no storage) or a longer window per contract. Customers may also request immediate deletion via the Console or by contacting support; legal holds will be honored.

- Model training / use of customer content: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts, responses, or attached files to train or fine-tune Redwood-managed models or third-party models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a written agreement. We may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry (token counts, error rates, latency metrics) to improve platform reliability and performance. Additionally, Redwood will not provide customer content to third parties for model training without prior customer consent.

Supporting links & artifacts:
- Data retention mapping: data-retention-table.xlsx (attached)
- SIG response PDF: Redwood_SIG_Response_2026-03-11.pdf (attached)
- Docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/security/data-retention and https://docs.redwood.ai/security/training-policy

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through these items and show where retention controls live in the Console.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
